title: Private House in Kaklebi  / Werkraum Design Architecture
text:
Private House in Kaklebi / Werkraum Design Architecture

The private house in Kaklebi, near Tbilisi, is composed of a series of timber-clad volumes rather than a single block, arranged to follow the slope of a wooded site and to preserve its existing mature trees. Distributed across multiple levels, the building reduces its own visual presence in the landscape while giving each level a distinct relationship to the terrain below.

title: The Portuguese Pavilion to Invite Four African Countries Through "Hands on the Ground" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
The Portuguese Pavilion to Invite Four African Countries Through "Hands on the Ground" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

The Portuguese Directorate-General for the Arts announced on November 16 the curatorial proposal that will represent the country at the 20th International Architecture Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia in 2027. The selected project was "Mãos ao Chão (Hands on the Ground)," an artistic and curatorial proposal by Joanna Alice Helm, Remígio van Eys Chilaule and Samuel de Brito Gonçalves. It was chosen from a limited competition among three teams. The other two proposals were "Analog Twins" by Alice Clanet-Hallard, Edgar Brito, Francisco Lobo and Romea Mury, and "Matéria Viva — Os materiais da construção portuguesa e o saber que resiste" by Helena Botelho. The evaluation committee was composed of Álvaro Domingues, Andreia Garcia, João Gomes da Silva, Mariana Pestana and Tânia Teixeira.

title: The Power of the Streets: Why Cities Remain Irreplaceable in the Digital Age
text:
The Power of the Streets: Why Cities Remain Irreplaceable in the Digital Age

Whether in Lisbon's medieval alleyways, along Haussmann's boulevards in Paris, on the wide avenues of car-oriented Chicago, or amid the metropolitan intensity of Avenida Paulista in São Paulo, different urban morphologies seem to give way to the same scene: crowds taking to the streets.

title: FORESTSCOPE / Sakakura Associates Architects and Engineers
text:
FORESTSCOPE / Sakakura Associates Architects and Engineers

A small spatial device that draws in and reflects the presence of the forest. Rather than simply looking out at the surrounding landscape, it directly brings in the image of the forest as it changes over time. After sunset, with projected images, it becomes a viewing hut that opens onto the outside world.

title: Abishkar Residence / SYSTEM architects - EKNC
text:
Abishkar Residence / SYSTEM architects - EKNC

ABISHKAR began not with the idea of a house, but with an attempt to understand the people who would inhabit it. At SYSTEM architects, design is approached as a participatory process. For this multi-generational home, planned for the parents and the families of their three sons, we began with a questionnaire about everyday life: how each person perceives space, what they value or avoid, their preferences, their need for privacy, and the kinds of spaces to which they feel naturally connected.

title: Sans Raison Renovation / Mountain Soil Interior Design
text:
Sans Raison Renovation / Mountain Soil Interior Design

Sans Raison is a 406-square-meter renovation project located in Jiading District, Shanghai. Originally an industrial building, the site retains much of its existing structure and the traces of its previous use. Rather than introducing an entirely new spatial arrangement, the design takes these existing conditions as a starting point, exploring how the building can accommodate new functions while retaining its original character.

title: Paper Stilt House / Esteban Uribe Architect
text:
Paper Stilt House / Esteban Uribe Architect

The Palafito de Papel is born from what already existed. It does not seek to be something new, but rather to belong, as if it had always existed in one of the most characteristic neighborhoods in the world: the stilt-house neighborhood of Castro, Chiloé. Wood and only wood. First, part of the existing structure was dismantled, as it was in a clear state of deterioration from decades of use and subsequent abandonment.

title: Floresta Building / MMBB Arquitetos + Rodrigo Oliveira Paisagismo
text:
Floresta Building / MMBB Arquitetos + Rodrigo Oliveira Paisagismo

From the very beginning, the design of Floresta aimed to organize the built volume around a central garden. Situated on a hillside that overlooks the São Paulo ridge on one side and the Tietê valley on the other, the apartments are aligned in two parallel blocks, transverse to the access street, with large windows facing both the internal garden and the neighboring urban panorama.

title: TS Building / De Rungs Arquitectos
text:
TS Building / De Rungs Arquitectos

Built in the 1980s as an office building, the property on Tolstoi Street had fallen into a clear state of disrepair. However, its open-plan layout and the condition of its structure provided the necessary conditions for its adaptation to a new residential program.

title: House in Besteiros / Rasura Arquitetos
text:
House in Besteiros / Rasura Arquitetos

A small ruin located on the boundary bordering the public road provides access to a steep plot organized in small terraces, densely populated with olive, chestnut, and orange trees. The search for tranquility and the ruin itself motivated the acquisition of the land and the desire to live in this place. From the very beginning, the design of the house aimed to preserve both the pre-existing structure and this atmosphere.

title: Soft Division Apartment / SABO project
text:
Soft Division Apartment / SABO project

A compact Lower East Side apartment was pared back and reimagined for a family of three. The design aims to soften divisions between spaces so the apartment is experienced as a central living room extending into surrounding alcoves.

title: McAnally Residence / MADDOCK
text:
McAnally Residence / MADDOCK

The stylishly designed house rises out of the sand dune, overlooking the ocean at Sunshine Beach, on the east coast of Australia, approximately 120km north of Brisbane.

title: Farmhouse in Novohradské Hory Reconstruction / Jan Vranovský
text:
Farmhouse in Novohradské Hory Reconstruction / Jan Vranovský

The reconstruction of a century-old farmhouse in the Czech Republic addresses the former disconnect between its living quarters and the surrounding garden while enabling comfortable year-round use. The intervention reverses the arrangement of the building's west wing by establishing a new center of activity within the former barn at the southern end, bringing it closer to natural light and connecting it to the garden. It also introduces a new ground-floor slab that serves as a heat distribution device while simultaneously helping to mitigate excessive ground moisture rising through the load-bearing walls.

title: Architecture as Evidence: Reading the Built Environment Through Forensic Investigation
text:
Architecture as Evidence: Reading the Built Environment Through Forensic Investigation

Architecture is commonly examined through its visible form, materials and spatial organisation. The physical fabric of a building can also retain evidence of events and alterations that are not apparent from its present appearance. Cracks, repairs and structural changes may indicate when and how a building was modified, while photographs and material fragments can provide further evidence about the circumstances surrounding those changes. Forensic investigation examines these traces, using the built environment and its surrounding records to establish how particular events, alterations or failures occurred.

title: Red Top Meadows Residential Treatment Facility / untitled architecture
text:
Red Top Meadows Residential Treatment Facility / untitled architecture

This project consists of a new building in a compound of existing structures at a residential treatment and therapeutic wilderness program located in a remote corner of Teton County, Wyoming. The program is for 12-18 year-old boys, sent there by the Wyoming state school or judicial system.

title: Lisbon Architecture Triennale Announces CO-OP as Theme for Its 2028 Edition
text:
Lisbon Architecture Triennale Announces CO-OP as Theme for Its 2028 Edition

The 8th Lisbon Architecture Triennale has announced CO-OP as the title of its 2028 edition, which will explore cooperation and its relationship with architecture, housing, production, and collective forms of living. Led by Chief Curator Joaquim Moreno, the upcoming edition will examine how cooperation can inform alternative ways of producing, building, and inhabiting spaces, while addressing questions of ownership, governance, and the common good. The Triennale will open on September 28, 2028, with a free three-day programme running through September 30 in Lisbon, Portugal.

title: Connecting Architectural Education with Specialized Fields at SCI-Arc
text:
Connecting Architectural Education with Specialized Fields at SCI-Arc

Artificial intelligence, climate challenges, and new media are changing how architects work and the knowledge they draw on. These shifts also raise questions about architectural education and how professional training can connect with specialized fields. SCI-Arc's new Accelerated Master of Science pathway offers one approach, allowing students to combine a professional architecture degree with a postgraduate degree in artificial intelligence, ecological design, media, or architectural pedagogy through one additional year of study.

title: Mecanoo Appointed to Transform Zutphen's Theatre Hanzehof into a New Cultural Center in the Netherlands
text:
Mecanoo Appointed to Transform Zutphen's Theatre Hanzehof into a New Cultural Center in the Netherlands

Following a European tender procedure, the Municipality of Zutphen, Netherlands, has appointed Mecanoo to transform the existing Theatre Hanzehof & Buitensociëteit into a cultural destination. The project, called Hanzehuis, was developed in collaboration with Hanzehof theater, de Muzehof center for the arts, and BIJ de Bieb library, and with ABT Consulting engineers and building services consultant Nelissen. It involves designing a new center for culture, knowledge and exchange, preserving the main historic building and introducing a new volume to accommodate cultural activities, education and community life under a single roof. Mecanoo contributed to the preparatory phase, and this appointment marks the transition to developing the design further with the professional team, the Municipality and the participating cultural organizations.

title: World Building of The Year and Interior of The Year Revealed at World Architecture Festival 2026
text:
World Building of The Year and Interior of The Year Revealed at World Architecture Festival 2026

The Prestige University by Sanjay Puri Architects in Indore, India, has been declared the World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival (WAF). The ultimate accolades of World Building of the Year, World Interior of the Year, and Future Project of the Year were announced as hundreds of architects from across the world convened at a grand finale Gala Dinner at the Broward County Convention Center in Florida. A host of Special Prizes, including the American Beauty Prize sponsored by RFACT, were also announced at the closing event to celebrate the nineteenth edition of the festival. The announcement follows the final day of WAF, in which prize winners across all 42 categories have been competing for the winning titles.

title: Holding Light: The Bahá’í Temple of South America in Santiago, Chile
text:
Holding Light: The Bahá’í Temple of South America in Santiago, Chile

Santiago spreads across the valley floor, and above its eastern edge, where the streets of Peñalolén give way to the foothills of the Andes, a pale form rises from a carved terrace: nine curved wings leaning toward one another. At dawn the building takes on the cold blue of the cordillera behind it. By midday it is a tent of white light, by late afternoon it turns gold, and after dark the sequence reverses: the temple becomes a lantern.

title: Powerhouse Parramatta / Moreau Kusunoki + Genton
text:
Powerhouse Parramatta / Moreau Kusunoki + Genton

Funded by the NSW Government and located on Dharug land, Powerhouse Parramatta is a major new landmark for Australia, making Western Sydney a global cultural destination. Its opening marks the most significant cultural infrastructure project since the Sydney Opera House. Powerhouse Parramatta, combined with the relocation of the Collection to Castle Hill, is a $A915 million project, including $A75 million in philanthropic contributions.

title: Yokohama Timber Wharf / Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture
text:
Yokohama Timber Wharf / Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture

Set in Rinko Park, the largest green space in Yokohama's Minato Mirai 21 district, Yokohama Timber Wharf is a multipurpose facility designed to connect architecture with the life of the waterfront park. Facing Yokohama Bay, the park's seaside promenade and broad lawns attract families, runners, and visitors throughout the year. The project brings dining and outdoor recreation support into this setting, creating a new gathering place and encouraging movement through Yokohama's coastal city center. DRAFT leads the development, while Taiju Yamashita Design and Architecture is responsible for the architectural design.

title: Why Material Lifespan Matters More Than Ever
text:
Why Material Lifespan Matters More Than Ever

A material's environmental footprint cannot be fully understood without considering its lifespan. A product with relatively low embodied carbon may require frequent replacement, additional installation resources, and repeated disposal over the life of a building. Conversely, a material with a higher initial impact may offer greater long-term value through its durability, reducing the need for future interventions. From this perspective, longevity goes beyond being a technical characteristic; it becomes an essential component of responsible architectural design.
